questions.q: Why is health declining even as medical science improves?
a: Modern diets rely on processed foods instead of traditional ones
People today exercise far less than any earlier generation
Vaccines and antibiotics have become less effective over time
Doctors no longer study nutrition during their training
questions.why: Lesson 1 says processed food replaced natural food, bringing age-related disease earlier in life.

questions.q: What went wrong when butter was replaced with margarine?
a: Margarine brought trans fats linked to health problems
Margarine contained too many natural minerals
Butter was found to be completely free of nutrients
Margarine made food spoil much faster
questions.why: Lesson 1 says the swap traded a natural fat for artificial trans fats.

questions.q: How do vegetable oils damage the brain, according to lesson 2?
a: Their trans fats disrupt antioxidant protection and allow oxidation
They remove all polyunsaturated fats from brain tissue
They block the brain from absorbing any water
They speed up the growth of new neural connections
questions.why: Lesson 2 explains that oxidation then lets free radicals damage vulnerable brain molecules.

questions.q: Why is sugar so easy to overconsume today?
a: Our sweetness receptors evolved when sugar was very scarce
Our bodies produce no receptors for sweet tastes at all
Modern sugar contains fewer calories than older sugar
The brain stops responding to sweetness after childhood
questions.why: Lesson 2 says modern overexposure overwhelms a system built for a low-sugar world.

questions.q: What are the four pillars of a healthy traditional diet?
a: Bone-in meat, organs, fermented or sprouted foods and fresh food
Lean poultry, dairy, whole grains and bottled supplements
Low calories, low fat, low sugar and frequent fasting
Raw vegetables, fruit, nuts and vegetable oils
questions.why: Lesson 3 lists meat on the bone, organs, fermented or sprouted food and fresh plants.
